subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract preserve paragraph seams with in-band separators where possible, carry explicit seam metadata through chunker/subscriber/coalescer/outbound, or accept this as a common-case partial repair?
rationale: The code proves the bug and the PR improves common paragraph splits, but the near-maxChars case cannot be fully solved by this text-only branch without an explicit maintainer choice about the delivery contract.

options.title: Require a complete shared fix
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit seam metadata
options.body: Ask contributors to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split boundary semantics through the streaming pipeline if text-only chunks cannot satisfy all invariants.

options.title: Accept a partial text repair
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally land the common-case improvement while leaving the near-limit boundary documented on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require a complete shared fix
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has strong recent history across coalescing, chunking hardening, and the affected streaming surfaces, making it the best available owner for the contract choice.
